text:
Justin Faulk is carrying a heavy load for Detroit and it shows on the scoresheet. The 34-year-old is up to 22:24 a night over his last ten games, more than two minutes above his season average, on a blue line that's playing a lot of hockey while the team's captain refuses to play until traded. And he's pointless in eight straight, with his expected points over that stretch (3.8) thin enough that we can't call it bad luck.

The rest of his game holds up better than the points. The Red Wings get 52.8% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, more than five points better than when he sits, and he's blocked 40 shots. Nine points in 24 games is about his talent range, not far off the league norm for a defenseman.

Evolving-Hockey had him just above replacement last season, with offense not his strength (his team's chance creation was bottom 4% with him on). Watch the minutes: if Detroit keeps leaning on him this hard, the points should come before the legs go.
